questions.question: Which nutrient is the body's major source of energy during high-intensity exercise? a) Carbohydrate b) Protein c) Vitamins d) Minerals
questions.solution_html:
• Which nutrient provides a significant amount of energy during lower -intensity, long-duration
  • exercise?
  • Answer: A. Fat
  • Answer: A. Reduces the use of amino acids for energy
  • During-exercise hydration
  • • Athletes should drink fluids at regular intervals according to thirst, sweat rate, exercise
  • intensity and environmental conditions.
  • • The aim is to replace fluid losses and minimize excessive dehydration during prolonged
  • exercise.
  • • Sports drinks containing carbohydrates and electrolytes are useful during endurance activities
  • lasting more than one hour because they provide energy and replace sodium losses.
  • • Athletes should develop an individualized hydration plan based on sweat rate, body weight
  • changes and previous training experience.
  • • Excessive drinking should be avoided because it can cause exercise -associated hyponatremia, a
  • dangerous decrease in blood sodium concentration.
  • • Hydration strategies should be practised during training before being used in competition.
  • Energy Density
  • • Energy density refers to the number of calories present per unit weight of food.
  • • Low-energy-density foods, such as vegetables, fruits and soups, provide fewer calories relative
  • to their weight and help promote fullness.
  • • High-energy-density foods, such as fried foods, sweets and foods rich in added fats, provide
  • more calories in smaller portions.
  • • Choosing nutrient-dense foods helps athletes meet their vitamin, mineral and fibre requirements
  • while controlling calorie intake.
  • • Appropriate portion sizes and healthy food choices support effective weight management.
  • Growth and Development
  • • Proteins are essential for the growth and development of muscles and other body tissues.
  • • Calcium, phosphorus and vitamin D support the development of strong bones and teeth.
  • • Carbohydrates and fats provide energy required for growth, physical activity and normal body
  • functions.
  • • Vitamins and minerals support brain development, hormonal functions and proper maturation.
  • • Adequate nutrition is especially important during childhood, adolescence and pregnancy.
  • During-exercise Phase
  • Dos
  • • Drink fluids regularly according to thirst, sweat rate and environmental conditions.
  • • Use carbohydrate-containing sports drinks or foods during prolonged endurance exercise when
  • appropriate.
  • • Replace electrolytes, particularly sodium, during prolonged exercise with substantial sweat
  • losses.
  • • Follow an individualized hydration and fueling plan practised during training.
  • • Monitor fatigue, thirst and other signs of dehydration.
  • Don'ts
  • • Do not ignore thirst or significant fluid losses.
  • • Avoid excessive fluid intake, which may cause exercise-associated hyponatremia.
  • • Do not consume large quantities of food that may cause gastrointestinal discomfort.
  • • Avoid experimenting with new sports drinks or supplements during competition.
  • • Do not rely on energy drinks as a substitute for proper hydration and nutrition.
questions.final_answer: • Do not rely on energy drinks as a substitute for proper hydration and nutrition.
